summary: Demand night for the geography channel. Added 4 topics from this month's breakouts: Dinorwig, the power station inside a Welsh mountain (re-sourced from the 7.5M half-time Short); what if the world became one country (2.95M); why North Korea is dark at night (1.23M); and why the Red Sea is called red (449K). Also gave 5 older topics references on their own idea.
why: The feed's best topics borrowed Chile's 10.6M as demand. The niche scan shows 484 Shorts from the last 30 days beating their channel 3x or more, and the new topics come from the biggest ones that fit the profile. Greenland, our first famous-place why_shaped Short, drew 1,135 views in about 14 hours, against 14 for Suez. That's views only, so no verdict.

findings.title: Breakout re-sourced: Britain's half-time power surge (7.52M on a 32.1K channel)
findings.detail: Told as the place behind it: Dinorwig, 1,800 MW inside Elidir Fawr, zero to full power in about 16 s.

findings.title: What if the whole world became one country: 2.95M on a 3.5K channel
findings.detail: The niche's biggest what-if. The topic is built on 193 UN members, 8.22B people (World Bank 2025) and 180 currencies.

findings.title: Greenland is our first Short past 1K views
findings.detail: 1,135 views and 20 likes in about 14 h; Suez had 14 views and Sahara 98. No stayed-to-watch data yet.

findings.title: The guard's daily merge limit is shared across channels
findings.detail: Paisa Panchayat's research branch was blocked on 19 Nov because the geography and tech research runs had already used the 2 merges. Raised to the owner.
